ending: The Wanderers finish with a rare greenhouse producing food under Finn's care, and their fortified settlement has become a recognized town. Joe remains in line for future guild leadership. The copied-wall conspiracy ends with the responsible Architects Guild leaders arrested, while Joe accepts a future commission to build a royal arena. He controls the captured forest cathedral and has Game Over contained beneath Pathfinder's Hall, where the creature's drained power supports his deity, but neither that threat nor the divine debt is resolved. Joe destroys the Grand Zoo's underground transport, trapping its arena, black market, and associated assassins. The crown clears him, but the Zoo now treats him as a blood-feud enemy. Aten, Mike, Jaxon, Jess, Joe's returning party, and his Ritualist coven remain active. Tara's secret reporting, the maintenance of Game Over's prison, further forest captures, the Zoo conflict, and the greenhouse's long-term risks remain open.
in_short: After people lose the ability to log out, Joe helps the Wanderers turn a damaged settlement into a sustainable town. His search for a durable food source leads through a hidden Wolfman refuge to a cult-held cathedral, which he captures for his indebted deity. The victory releases Game Over, a permanently lethal Burning Mind fragment that Joe contains and drains rather than destroys. He develops mana batteries, forms a Ritualist coven, and builds a rare greenhouse that begins producing food. The Architects Guild frames the Wanderers over a copied defensive wall, but its leaders expose their own attack and are arrested. Queen Marie then sends Joe against the Grand Zoo. Joe sabotages its underground Bloodsport Arena and destroys its transport system, trapping the black market below. The crown clears him, while the Zoo declares a blood feud. The town and greenhouse survive, but Game Over, Joe's divine debt, Tara's covert reporting, and the Zoo remain unresolved.

recaps.text: Previously: Joe became a prominent leader among the Wanderers through his ritual construction, healing, and service during the recent war. His allies rely on him both as a combatant and as a builder capable of creating vital infrastructure. His wartime actions included saving King Henry, and the consequences of that rescue remain important as the Wanderers begin rebuilding.

King Henry honors Joe for his wartime service, but the queen questions how Joe managed the king's resurrection. At his patron's altar, Joe learns that the resurrection placed the deity under review and created a debt of thirteen million units of divine energy. Joe keeps his allegiance and accepts responsibility for repayment, although he loses the divine increase to his mana pool. At the same time, everyone discovers that logging out is no longer possible. The Wanderers must therefore rebuild their ruined settlement as a permanent home. Joe and Mike use exacting, mana-heavy rituals to create barracks, and Joe later learns to make and reuse magical building plans. Jaxon returns with living hand-weapons and introduces Jess, who quickly proves useful in administration and logistics. After Joe's party clears a salt dungeon, the guild gains a productive mine. Aten then tasks the group with establishing lasting food production for ten thousand people. Joe and Jess settle on a greenhouse project, but the Architects Guild will neither sell its proprietary plans nor provide materials quickly. Joe begins developing his own blueprint methods and identifies a former elven region as the best lead.

While traveling toward the greenhouse lead, Joe's party destroys plague-bearing lions before they can infect a refugee camp, then defeats a giant scorpion. Joe's attempt to advance his mana control leaves his mana dispersed through his body, but also makes one defense faster to cast. A masked assassin corners the party over Joe's earlier rare-creature dealings, and Joe avoids execution by accepting an obligation to capture a coffee elemental. He later heals a poisoned farming caravan and converts its shrine, gaining followers for his indebted patron. The group enters a forest far above its level in search of food-production knowledge. Its first attempt ends when a massive treant kills Joe. After respawning, he develops a spell and ritual designed to attack rooted plants. On the return expedition, a Rose Beast kills Alexis, whom Joe immediately resurrects. A Wolfman warrior recognizes Jaxon and guides the party to a concealed refugee settlement. Its elder offers access to the forest's advanced growth houses on one condition: Joe's party must clear a nearby human cult while preserving the refuge's secrecy.

The Wolfman refuge reveals a vast greenhouse that is larger inside than outside. Its blueprint will be Joe's reward if his underleveled party defeats the cult occupying a nearby cathedral. Observation shows that the cathedral's humming compels people and strengthens its hierophant, so Joe plans to capture the building for his own deity and strip away those advantages. Because the conversion requires far more mana than his party can provide, Joe revises a dangerous enchantment into a rechargeable mana battery. He also accepts a long-term construction agreement with the Wanderers and forms a small Ritualist coven from volunteers willing to help power building rituals. The coven successfully tests a permanent battery system in the cleared salt mine. Returning to the forest with batteries and a diversion plan, Joe's group draws the cult's defenders outside and enters the cathedral. Joe completes the conversion while his allies hold off returning cultists. The captured site transfers divine energy to his patron, but the hierophant reveals that its altar has been binding a fragment of the Burning Mind. The restraint dissolves, releasing Game Over, a creature whose victims can suffer permanent death.

Game Over overwhelms the cathedral's divine protectors and rapidly recovers from Joe's attacks. The captured hierophant is consumed, completing the cult's defeat, but Joe can only pull the creature underground and design a prison around it. He later installs a stronger containment ritual beneath Pathfinder's Hall, draining energy from Game Over into his deity while leaving the creature alive and dangerous. The Wolfman elder awards the promised greenhouse plan, and Joe replaces its damaged copy by scanning the original. Its rare design demands costly materials and careful substitutions. Tara helps find a workable frame and recognizes the wider value of Joe's batteries, while secretly passing information about him to an unknown party. Elsewhere, Aten and Mike ask Joe to copy a defensive-wall blueprint supplied by an apparent informant. The source is actually participating in an Architects Guild sting intended to produce a treason charge. Joe continues gathering greenhouse components, including enchanted glass and a rare core, and settles his obligation to the rare-creature organization, receiving a coffee elemental. He also witnesses the Grand Zoo's illicit underground Bloodsport Arena and its concealed transport system.

Joe, Aten, and the coven complete the rare ever-growth greenhouse. It can produce large amounts of food and herbs, but neglect could turn it into a dungeon and its growth will eventually drain the surrounding land. A ballista attack kills Aten during the ritual, and Joe resurrects him. Expecting further attacks, the Wanderers rapidly erect the copied defensive wall and reach the status of a recognized town. Finn takes charge of the greenhouse and begins establishing crops. A prince then warns that the wall's protected design exposes the guild to a treason accusation. Joe dismantles it before the Royal Guard arrives, even after an inhaled agent incapacitates the rest of the guild. The Architects Guild leaders accompanying the guard reveal knowledge that ties them to the attack and false charge, leading to their arrest. Queen Marie orders Joe to investigate the Grand Zoo's black market and assassins in exchange for resolving the remaining accusation. Joe prepares an escape ritual and special reagents for the mission. A separate water ritual unexpectedly uncovers Jaxon alive in a swamp, after which Joe heals him and returns him to the guild.

At the Grand Zoo, Joe secretly establishes ritual links to the Bloodsport Arena despite tighter surveillance and the confiscation of his storage ring. Robert, the arena's ringleader, recognizes that Joe's purchases could support powerful ritual work and places him under close observation. Joe consumes a legendary intelligence injection, then uses its debilitating effects as cover while maintaining a magical connection to the arena. He triggers his scanning ability and a concealing fog, locates the underground transport enchantment through magical synesthesia, and briefly takes control of the route between the Zoo and the city's main square. Rather than preserve that access, he destroys the enchantment with acid, trapping the arena, black market, nobles, and assassins underground. The crown confirms that he found and destroyed the unique building, clearing his record and counting the act toward his path to nobility, though he failed the separate objective of securing independent two-way access. King Henry and Queen Marie demand accountability from nobles linked to the black market, and the queen voids coercive work obligations. Joe agrees to build a legitimate arena if the crown supplies the materials. The Grand Zoo now regards him as a blood-feud enemy.
